rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

WITH customer_transactions_cleaned AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','debit','wd','payment','purchase') THEN -1.0 * txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit','cr','refund') THEN 1.0 * txn_amount
      ELSE 1.0 * txn_amount
    END AS txn_amount_signed
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND length(txn_date) = 10
    AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-'
    AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-'
    AND cast(substr(txn_date,1,4) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1000 AND 9999
    AND cast(substr(txn_date,6,2) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1 AND 12
    AND cast(substr(txn_date,9,2) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1 AND 31
),
customer_monthly_transaction_sums AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01') AS month_start,
    SUM(txn_amount_signed) AS month_txn_sum
  FROM customer_transactions_cleaned
  GROUP BY customer_id, month_start
),
customer_date_ranges AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(min(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01')) AS first_month_start,
    date(max(substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01')) AS last_month_start
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND length(txn_date) = 10
    AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-'
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
month_numbers AS (
  SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
  UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
  UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
  UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
  UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
  UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
  UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
  UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
  UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
  UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
  UNION ALL SELECT 60

generated_months AS (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    date(r.first_month_start, '+' || n.n || ' months') AS month_start
  FROM customer_date_ranges r
  JOIN month_numbers n ON date(r.first_month_start, '+' || n.n || ' months') <= r.last_month_start
),
monthly_with_values AS (
  SELECT
    gm.customer_id,
    gm.month_start,
    date(gm.month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
    COALESCE(m.month_txn_sum, 0.0) AS month_txn_sum
  FROM generated_months gm
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_transaction_sums m
    ON m.customer_id = gm.customer_id
   AND m.month_start = gm.month_start
),
running AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start,
    month_end,
    month_txn_sum,
    -- running total up to current month
    SUM(month_txn_sum) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total
  FROM monthly_with_values
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  month_start AS month_start_date,
  month_end AS month_end_date,
  ROUND(running_total, 10) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly change is simply the month_txn_sum (rounded)
  ROUND(month_txn_sum, 10) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance equals closing_balance (running total)
  ROUND(running_total, 10) AS cumulative_balance
FROM running
ORDER BY customer_id, year, month

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH months AS (
  -- use month labels that match actual txn_date patterns present in the DB (use '2020-01' etc. but restrict by available txn rows below)
  SELECT '2020-01' AS month_label UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-02' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-03' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-05' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-08' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-09' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-11' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-12'
),
all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
cust_month_sums AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(txn_date,1,7) AS month_label,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawals
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE substr(txn_date,1,4) = '2020'
    AND (txn_type = 'deposit' OR txn_type = 'withdrawal')
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(txn_date,1,7)
),
customer_month_balance AS (
  SELECT
    a.customer_id,
    m.month_label,
    COALESCE(cms.sum_deposits,0) - COALESCE(cms.sum_withdrawals,0) AS month_end_balance
  FROM all_customers a
  CROSS JOIN months m
  LEFT JOIN cust_month_sums cms
    ON cms.customer_id = a.customer_id
    AND cms.month_label = m.month_label
),
month_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    SUM(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(month_end_balance) AS average_month_end_balance
  FROM customer_month_balance
  GROUP BY month_label
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    positive_customer_count,
    average_month_end_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, month_label ASC) AS rn_high,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, month_label ASC) AS rn_low
  FROM month_aggregates
),
picked AS (
  SELECT 'highest_positive_count_month' AS role, month_label, positive_customer_count, average_month_end_balance FROM ranked WHERE rn_high = 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'lowest_positive_count_month' AS role, month_label, positive_customer_count, average_month_end_balance FROM ranked WHERE rn_low = 1
),
diffs AS (
  SELECT
    p.*,
    (SELECT average_month_end_balance FROM picked WHERE role = 'highest_positive_count_month')
    -
    (SELECT average_month_end_balance FROM picked WHERE role = 'lowest_positive_count_month') AS avg_difference
  FROM picked p
)
SELECT
  month_label,
  positive_customer_count,
  average_month_end_balance,
  role,
  CASE WHEN role = 'highest_positive_count_month' THEN avg_difference ELSE NULL END AS difference_between_averages
FROM diffs
ORDER BY CASE WHEN role = 'highest_positive_count_month' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_txn_monthly_net AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- anchor month to first day of month in ISO YYYY-MM-DD using txn_date
  date(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)) || '-01') AS month_period,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
      ELSE ct.txn_amount
    END
  ) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_period
),
customer_monthly_closing_balance_59 AS (
SELECT
  cmn.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmn.month_period AS month_period,
  cmn.monthly_net AS monthly_net,
  SUM(cmn.monthly_net) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cmn.customer_id
    ORDER BY cmn.month_period
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_txn_monthly_net cmn
),
customer_latest_month_growth AS (
SELECT
  cmcb.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmcb.month_period AS latest_month_period,
  COALESCE(cmcb_prior.closing_balance, 0) AS closing_balance_prior,
  COALESCE(cmcb.closing_balance, 0) AS closing_balance_current,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(cmcb_prior.closing_balance, 0) = 0 THEN COALESCE(cmcb.closing_balance, 0) * 100.0
    ELSE (COALESCE(cmcb.closing_balance, 0) - COALESCE(cmcb_prior.closing_balance, 0)) / COALESCE(cmcb_prior.closing_balance, 0)
  END AS growth_rate
FROM
  customer_monthly_closing_balance_59 cmcb
LEFT JOIN
  customer_monthly_closing_balance_59 cmcb_prior
ON
  cmcb.customer_id = cmcb_prior.customer_id
  AND (
    -- assume month_period formatted so prior period is lexically less; join to the immediately prior period by matching month_period values:
    cmcb_prior.month_period = (
      SELECT month_period FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance_59 sub
      WHERE sub.customer_id = cmcb.customer_id
        AND sub.month_period < cmcb.month_period
      ORDER BY sub.month_period DESC
      LIMIT 1
    )
  )
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_customers_considered,
  COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FILTER (WHERE growth_rate > 0.05) AS customers_with_growth_gt_5pct,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) = 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE (COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FILTER (WHERE growth_rate > 0.05) * 100.0) / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)
  END AS percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5pct
FROM customer_latest_month_growth

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_cumulative_balance_by_cutoff AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    date(ct.txn_date) AS cutoff_date,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(txn_amount),0)
     FROM customer_transactions ct2
     WHERE ct2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
       AND date(ct2.txn_date) <= date(ct.txn_date)
    ) AS cumulative_balance
  FROM customer_transactions ct
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, date(ct.txn_date)
),
calendar_months_from_transactions AS (
  SELECT
    date(substr(txn_date,1,10), 'start of month') AS month_start_date,
    strftime('%Y-%m', date(substr(txn_date,1,10), 'start of month')) AS month_ym
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY month_start_date, month_ym
)
SELECT
  cm.month_ym AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(ccb.cumulative_balance,0) < 0 THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(ccb.cumulative_balance,0) END) AS total_balance
FROM calendar_months_from_transactions cm
LEFT JOIN customer_cumulative_balance_by_cutoff ccb
  ON ccb.cutoff_date = date(cm.month_start_date, '-1 day')
-- exclude the first month in the dataset (use first month only as baseline)
WHERE cm.month_start_date > (SELECT MIN(month_start_date) FROM calendar_months_from_transactions)
GROUP BY cm.month_ym
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.

WITH customer_transactions_base AS (
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_date AS txn_date,
  txn_type AS txn_type,
  txn_amount AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_transactions_normalized AS (
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date, 7,4) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,2)) 
    AS txn_date,
  CAST(customer_transactions.txn_amount AS REAL) AS txn_amount,
  customer_transactions.txn_type AS txn_type,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date, 7,4) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,2))) AS INTEGER) 
    AS calendar_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date, 7,4) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,2))) AS INTEGER) 
    AS month_number,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date, 7,4) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,2)))) 
    AS month_start_date,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date, 7,4) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,2))), '+1 month', '-1 day') 
    AS month_end_date
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_daily_end_balance AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id,
  DATE(ct.txn_date) AS date,
  -- compute signed txn_amount: deposits positive, others negative
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      ELSE -ct.txn_amount
    END
  ) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ct.customer_id
    ORDER BY DATE(ct.txn_date) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS end_of_day_balance,
  -- flag whether the transaction's month is the first month the customer transacted
  CASE
    WHEN strftime('%Y-%m', DATE(ct.txn_date)) = strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(DATE(ct.txn_date)) OVER (PARTITION BY ct.customer_id))
    THEN 1 ELSE 0
  END AS is_first_month_flag
FROM customer_transactions AS ct
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_daily_balance AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id AS customer_id,
  d.date AS date,
  AVG(e.end_of_day_balance) AS rolling_30d_avg_balance
FROM
  customer_daily_end_balance e
JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      date
    FROM
      customer_daily_end_balance
    GROUP BY
      customer_id,
      date
  ) d
  ON e.customer_id = d.customer_id
     AND DATE(e.date) BETWEEN DATE(d.date, '-29 days') AND DATE(d.date)
GROUP BY
  d.customer_id,
  d.date
HAVING
  COUNT(e.date) = 30
),
customer_monthly_max_30d_avg AS (
SELECT
  v.customer_id,
  substr(v.date,1,7) AS month,
  COALESCE(MAX(
    CASE
      WHEN r.rolling_30d_avg_balance IS NULL THEN 0
      WHEN r.rolling_30d_avg_balance < 0 THEN 0
      ELSE CAST(floor(r.rolling_30d_avg_balance) AS INTEGER)
    END
  ), 0) AS monthly_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM
  customer_daily_end_balance AS v
LEFT JOIN
  customer_30day_rolling_avg_daily_balance AS r
  ON v.customer_id = r.customer_id
  AND v.date = r.date
GROUP BY
  v.customer_id,
  month
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  SUM(m.monthly_max_30day_avg_balance) AS monthly_total_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM
  customer_monthly_max_30d_avg AS m
JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', date)) AS first_month
  FROM customer_daily_end_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS first_months
  ON m.customer_id = first_months.customer_id
WHERE
  m.month <> first_months.first_month
GROUP BY
  m.month
ORDER BY
  m.month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD; assume input like '2020-1-2' or '2020-01-02' or '2020/01/02'
  substr(
    printf('%04d-%02d-%02d',
      CAST(strftime('%Y', replace(replace(txn_date,'/','-'),'T',' ')) AS INTEGER),
      CAST(strftime('%m', replace(replace(txn_date,'/','-'),'T',' ')) AS INTEGER),
      CAST(strftime('%d', replace(replace(txn_date,'/','-'),'T',' ')) AS INTEGER)
    ),

  SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),

  customer_transaction_date_range c
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      date(min_txn_date, '+' || (n.n) || ' days') AS day,

    FROM
      customer_transaction_date_range c2,
      (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29 UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59 UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64 UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69 UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74 UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79 UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84 UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89 UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94 UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99) n
    WHERE date(min_txn_date, '+' || n.n || ' days') <= max_txn_date
  ) d ON d.customer_id = c.customer_id
  LEFT JOIN (

ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.

SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name,
  e.event_type,
  t.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier t
  ON e.event_type = t.event_type

),

  event_name
FROM

),

  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
   AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
   AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
   AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken w
    ON w.match_id = b.match_id
   AND w.over_id = b.over_id
   AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
   AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
  GROUP BY
    b.bowler,
    b.match_id
),
career_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    bm.bowler AS bowler,
    SUM(bm.balls_bowled_in_match) AS total_balls_bowled,
    SUM(bm.runs_conceded_off_bat_in_match) AS total_runs_conceded_off_bat,
    SUM(bm.wickets_in_match) AS total_wickets
  FROM bowler_match_level_metrics bm
  GROUP BY bm.bowler
),
best_per_match AS (
  -- For each bowler find matches with max wickets
  SELECT
    bm.bowler,
    bm.match_id,
    bm.wickets_in_match,
    bm.runs_conceded_off_bat_in_match
  FROM bowler_match_level_metrics bm
  JOIN (
    SELECT bowler, MAX(wickets_in_match) AS max_wk
    FROM bowler_match_level_metrics
    GROUP BY bowler
  ) mw ON bm.bowler = mw.bowler AND bm.wickets_in_match = mw.max_wk
),
best_per_bowler AS (
  -- From those, pick minimal runs conceded
  SELECT
    bpm.bowler,
    MIN(bpm.runs_conceded_off_bat_in_match) AS min_runs
  FROM best_per_match bpm
  GROUP BY bpm.bowler
),
chosen_match AS (
  -- From remaining ties pick smallest match_id
  SELECT
    bpm.bowler,
    bpm.match_id,
    bpm.wickets_in_match,
    bpm.runs_conceded_off_bat_in_match
  FROM best_per_match bpm
  JOIN best_per_bowler bpb
    ON bpm.bowler = bpb.bowler
   AND bpm.runs_conceded_off_bat_in_match = bpb.min_runs
  JOIN (
    SELECT bowler, MIN(match_id) AS chosen_match_id
    FROM best_per_match
    GROUP BY bowler
  ) cm ON bpm.bowler = cm.bowler AND bpm.match_id = cm.chosen_match_id
)
SELECT
  p.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  COALESCE(ca.total_wickets, 0) AS total_wickets,
  COALESCE(ca.total_balls_bowled, 0) AS total_balls_bowled,
  COALESCE(ca.total_runs_conceded_off_bat, 0) AS total_runs_conceded_off_bat,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ca.total_balls_bowled,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(ca.total_runs_conceded_off_bat AS REAL) / (ca.total_balls_bowled / 6.0))
  END AS economy_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ca.total_wickets,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(ca.total_balls_bowled AS REAL) / ca.total_wickets)
  END AS strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN cm.match_id IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE (CAST(cm.wickets_in_match AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(cm.runs_conceded_off_bat_in_match AS TEXT))
  END AS best_figures
FROM player p
LEFT JOIN career_aggregates ca ON p.player_id = ca.bowler
